scope: Theorem 6.1 (Radius-weighted block estimate) of the manuscript “Subsphere methods for memory-sample lower bounds in noiseless Gaussian regression” (preprints/Subsphere-methods-for-memory-sample-lower-bounds-in-noiseless-Gaussian-regression-September-27-2026/paper.pdf), one of the manuscripts of result family 140 of openai/math at commit 1581d4cbdd69. The statement is quoted verbatim from the text that pdftotext 24.02.0 (-raw -enc UTF-8) extracts from the PDF (SHA-256 a645c0aa5ef45578), with whitespace normalised, and was found there under this heading on PDF page 16. Text extraction flattens typeset mathematics (superscripts, subscripts, fractions, large operators, delimiters), so the quote can read differently from the typeset statement and can carry characters with no Unicode meaning; the PDF is authoritative. Finding the quote shows that the manuscript states it, not that it is true. AMVO has checked nothing about this claim.
statement: There are absolute constants C ≥ 1 and d∗ such that the following holds for every integer d ≥ d∗. Put k = m = ⌊d/16⌋, a = d/16. Let W ≥ 1, let V be a nonempty finite set with |V| ≤ W, and let κv : Rk×d × Rk → [0, 1] be Borel functions with P v∈V κv ≤ 1. For Borel gv : Sd−1 → [0, 1], set gin(s) = EX X v∈V κv(X, Xs)gv(s), where X has k independent N(0, Id) rows. For every integer n with d/2 ≤ n ≤ d, Bn(gin) ≤ W1/m Cd max v∈V Bn−2(gv). (32) If ϵ > 0, π is any probability measure on Sd−1 and gπ(s) = Z 1{arccos⟨u,s⟩≤ϵ} π(du), then, in the same range of n, Bn(gπ) ≤ Cd ϵa . (33)
